newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to cut 1998 deficit by 25 trln lire - union.
newsitem.headline: Italy to cut 1998 deficit by 25 trln lire - union.

text.p: The Italian government intends to cut the public sector deficit by 25 trillion lire in next year's budget, with two-thirds coming from spending cuts and one third from increased revenue, a union leader said.
Sergio D'Antoni, leader of the CISL trade union confederation, said the figures were outlined in a meeting between the government and trade union leaders on Tuesday evening.
"This is what they told us," D'Antoni told Reuters.
The 1998 budget plan is contained in a draft of the government's three-year economic strategy, known as the DPEF, broad details of which were given to the union leaders.
D'Antoni said the breakdown in the 1998 budget equated to eight trillion lire in increased revenues and 17 trillion in spending cuts.
"This is not fairly balanced and the unions want it (the breakdown) to be half and half," said D'Antoni.

D'Antoni said the government had not discussed cuts in social welfare spending. "Nothing was said. But it is clear that the more you cut spending the more you have to cut social (welfare) spending," he added.

Sergio Cofferati, leader of Italy's largest trade union confederation, CGIL, said earlier that he too was unhappy with the proposed breakdown between spending cuts and increased revenues in the 1998 budget.
The government is to hold a formal round of talks with trade union leaders and employers on Thursday afternoon on the DPEF in which more details will be made available.
"Tomorrow there will be as general meeting and on that occasion they will explain the contents to us," said D'Antoni.
Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni said on Wednesday the government would, appropve the DPEF at a cabinet meeting.
Negotiations between the government, trade unions and employers on reforming Italy's welfare state are due to move into high gear after the DPEF has been approved.
